system_overview: This specification models a sliding block puzzle, commonly known as Klotski. The puzzle consists of a rectangular board with several pieces of various shapes that can slide horizontally and vertically into empty spaces. The goal is to move a designated large piece to a target position by sliding other pieces out of the way. The model checker explores the full state space of reachable board configurations to determine whether the goal position is achievable.
actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The system consists of a rectangular grid board and a collection of rigid pieces (blocks) of various sizes and shapes placed on the board. Each piece occupies one or more grid cells. There are also empty cells (not occupied by any piece) that allow pieces to slide. The key puzzle variant defined is the Klotski configuration, which uses a 4-wide by 5-tall grid with ten pieces: one 2-by-2 square block, several 1-by-2 and 2-by-1 rectangular blocks, and several 1-by-1 unit blocks.
state_variables: The system tracks the current board configuration, which is the set of all pieces currently on the board, where each piece is itself a set of grid positions it occupies. Each grid position is a coordinate pair within the bounds of the board.
initial_state: The board starts in the standard Klotski starting configuration. The ten pieces are placed in their traditional positions on the 4-by-5 grid, with two empty cells remaining.
actions: In each step, one empty cell is selected. For each direction (up, down, left, right), if there is an adjacent piece in that direction, the system considers sliding that entire piece one cell in the opposite direction (toward the empty cell). The move is valid only if the resulting position of the piece remains entirely within the board bounds and does not overlap with any other piece. The board configuration is updated by replacing the old piece position with the new one. Multiple possible moves may exist in each state (one for each combination of empty cell and valid sliding direction), creating nondeterministic branching.
safety_properties: The board must always be a valid set of non-overlapping pieces on the grid (type correctness). The goal invariant states that the 2-by-2 block has NOT reached its target position (bottom-center of the board). When the model checker finds a violation of this invariant, it has found a solution path from the initial configuration to the goal.
model_bounds: The board dimensions are fixed at width 4 and height 5. All grid positions are integer coordinate pairs within these bounds. The number and shapes of pieces are fixed by the chosen puzzle variant (Klotski uses 10 pieces). The README notes that TLC finds 25,955 distinct states for the Klotski variant.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses an invariant-violation technique for puzzle solving: the goal condition is stated as an invariant (the goal has NOT been reached), and a counterexample trace produced by the model checker represents a solution to the puzzle. The specification also supports other puzzle variants (Pennant with 1,398 states, Ma's Puzzle with 110,804 states) by changing the piece definitions, board dimensions, and goal conditions.
